title: Another Code: Two Memories
subtitle: A letter from a missing father
summary: Another Code: Two Memories is Cing's Nintendo DS mystery adventure about thirteen-year-old Ashley Mizuki Robbins. body: Another Code: Two Memories is Cing's Nintendo DS mystery adventure about thirteen-year-old Ashley Mizuki Robbins. A letter leads her to Blood Edward Island in search of the father she believed was dead. The player moves Ashley through three-dimensional locations while examining closer views, objects and photographs. Known as Trace Memory in North America, the game places a quiet investigation inside the unfamiliar shape of Nintendo's new handheld. Looking carefully and trying the machine's different inputs become part of discovering what happened to her family.

The lower screen provides an overhead view for moving Ashley, using either the stylus or the directional pad. The upper screen supplies a closer image of the current location. Selecting something worth examining brings it into the investigation, where an ordinary object may conceal the next clue. Ashley also carries an electronic device called the DAS, named DTS in North America. It reads data cards and stores photographs. Information is therefore something the player can collect, revisit and compare rather than simply hear once in a conversation.

Puzzles draw on the touchscreen and microphone, asking the player to consider the DS itself as a set of tools. Ashley's camera can retain a limited collection of pictures, making a photograph useful as evidence as well as a record of a place. These actions suit the story's concern with uncertain memories: an answer may depend on examining something again with another piece of information. Cing makes the small, personal act of handling a portable machine feel appropriate to a young character investigating her own history.
